reducing-air-pollutants-s1.title: A coal power plant before and after new pollution controls

table.caption: Yearly emissions from one coal power plant, in metric tons (invented data for practice)

reducing-air-pollutants-s2.title: A passage on a sulfur dioxide trading program
reducing-air-pollutants-s2.passage: A state council is debating a plan to cut sulfur dioxide from its twelve coal power plants. Under the plan, the state sets a total cap on SO2 for all plants together and lowers it by 5% each year. Each plant receives permits for its share. A plant that cuts its emissions below its permits, for example by installing a scrubber or switching to low-sulfur coal, may sell the extra permits to a plant that finds cutting more expensive. Supporters say the cap guarantees the total cut while letting the cheapest cuts happen first. Critics worry that a plant buying many permits could keep polluting its own neighborhood, and they ask the council to add a limit for each plant as well as the total cap.

items.q: What percent of the plant's sulfur dioxide does the wet scrubber remove?

mistakes.why: 5% is the share that is left (2,000 of 40,000). The scrubber removes the other 95%.
That is the fraction. Multiply by 100 for a percent: 95%.

items.q: Which pollutant's emissions were cut by the largest percent?
options: Sulfur dioxide, cut by the wet scrubber
Particulate matter
Nitrogen oxides, by a lower burner temperature
Carbon dioxide, by the new controls

why.correct: Particulates fell from 8,000 to 80 metric tons, a 99% cut. SO2 fell 95%, NOx 20%, and CO2 0%.
options: The scrubber cut SO2 by 95%, a little less than the particulate cut.
Right: 80 of 8,000 is left, a 99% cut.
NOx fell from 12,000 to 9,600, just 20%.
CO2 did not change; none of these devices removes it.

items.q: Why did the new controls not lower the plant's CO2?
options: The devices remove SO2 and particles, not CO2
The scrubber turns the SO2 into extra CO2
CO2 is a particle that the precipitator missed
Less CO2 forms when coal burns at a lower temperature

why.correct: Scrubbers and precipitators remove SO2 and particles. CO2 is the main product of burning carbon in coal, and the plant burns the same coal, so it releases the same CO2.
options: Right: burning the same coal makes the same CO2.
Limestone scrubbers release a little CO2, but that is not why the CO2 stayed level here.
CO2 is a gas, not a particle.
Lowering burner temperature cuts NOx; CO2 still forms from the carbon.

items.q: Lowering the burner temperature cut NOx by 20%. Why does burning at a lower temperature reduce NOx?
options: A cooler flame burns off the nitrogen in the coal first
Lower heat turns NOx into sulfur dioxide
A cooler flame makes the scrubber work on NOx too
Less air nitrogen joins oxygen in a cooler flame

why.correct: Most NOx forms when nitrogen and oxygen from the air combine at very high temperatures. A cooler flame makes less of that reaction happen.
options: Most NOx comes from nitrogen in the air, and cooling does not burn anything off.
Nitrogen cannot turn into sulfur.
The scrubber targets SO2; the NOx cut comes from the flame itself.
Right: NOx formation rises steeply with flame temperature.

items.q: What is the main claim made by the plan's supporters?
options: Each plant should be required to install the same scrubber
SO2 should be cut mainly to slow global climate warming
A cap with trading cuts SO2 at low cost
Plants that buy permits will clean up their neighborhoods

why.correct: Supporters say the cap guarantees the total cut while trading lets plants make the cheapest cuts first.
options: The plan lets plants choose how to cut; it does not require one device.
The passage says nothing of warming; SO2 is cut to protect health and lakes and forests.
Right: that is the supporters' claim.
That is the opposite of the critics' worry.

items.q: What assumption underlies the critics' concern?
options: A cap will fail to lower the total SO2 from the twelve plants
SO2 harms people most near the plant that releases it
Scrubbers do not remove SO2 from a plant's exhaust
Low-sulfur coal costs more than ordinary coal everywhere

why.correct: The critics assume that SO2 harms people mostly near the plant that releases it, so a plant that buys permits could leave its own neighbors with dirty air even while the state total falls.
options: Critics do not dispute the total cut; they worry about where it happens.
Right: the worry only makes sense if local emissions matter locally.
The passage presents scrubbers as a way to cut SO2.
Cost is the supporters' topic; the critics are concerned with local harm.

items.q: Which evidence would best support the supporters' claim?
options: A past cap-and-trade plan met its goal for less money
One plant's neighbors had more asthma after it bought permits
Coal plants also release mercury and CO2
Some states use wind farms instead of coal plants

why.correct: The claim is that trading lowers the cost of a guaranteed cut. Data showing a cap-and-trade program met its target at lower cost than expected would support it directly.
options: Right: that tests the cost claim directly.
That supports the critics, not the supporters.
True, but it says nothing about whether trading cuts SO2 cheaply.
That is about energy choices, not the cost of the cap.

items.q: Is the plan described in the passage a policy or a technology?
options: A technology, because scrubbers are one way to meet it
A technology, because it uses permits that can be sold
Neither, because it does not name a pollutant to cut
A policy, because it is a rule plants follow

why.correct: A cap with tradable permits is a rule set by the state, so it is a policy. Scrubbers and low-sulfur coal are the technologies plants may choose to meet it.
options: Scrubbers are a technology a plant may use, but the plan itself is a rule.
A permit is a legal right to emit, part of a rule, not a device.
The plan names SO2 directly.
Right: the cap and permits are a rule; scrubbers are the technology.

items.q: Which device in a car changes carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and unburned hydrocarbons into less harmful gases?
options: A wet scrubber
An electrostatic precipitator
A catalytic converter
A vapor recovery nozzle

why.correct: A catalytic converter uses metal catalysts to turn CO into CO2, NOx into nitrogen gas, and hydrocarbons into CO2 and water.
options: Scrubbers are used on smokestacks to remove SO2.
Precipitators remove particles from smokestack gases.
Right: its catalysts change CO, NOx and hydrocarbons into less harmful gases.
These nozzles capture gasoline vapor at the pump, not exhaust.

items.q: How does an electrostatic precipitator remove particles from a smokestack?
options: It sprays a limestone slurry that reacts with the particles
It charges particles and collects them on plates
It forces the gas through fabric bags that trap the particles
It uses a catalyst to change particles into harmless gases

why.correct: It gives the particles an electric charge, then collects them on plates with the opposite charge. The plates are shaken clean and the ash is collected.
options: A limestone spray is a scrubber, used mainly for SO2.
Right: opposite charges attract the particles out of the gas.
Fabric bags describe a baghouse filter, a different device.
Catalysts change gases in car exhaust; they do not remove particles.

items.q: A wet scrubber sprays a mixture of water and crushed limestone into a coal plant's exhaust. What does it remove, and how?
options: SO2, which reacts with limestone and is caught
CO2, which the water turns into oxygen
Carbon monoxide, which the limestone burns off
Ozone, which the water vapor breaks apart

why.correct: SO2 is an acidic gas. It reacts with the limestone in the spray and is captured as a solid calcium compound (often made into gypsum) instead of leaving the stack.
options: Right: the base in the spray neutralizes the acidic SO2.
Water does not turn CO2 into oxygen, and scrubbers target SO2.
Limestone does not burn CO; catalytic converters handle CO in cars.
Ozone is not emitted by the stack; it forms later in the air.

items.q: What does a vapor recovery nozzle on a gas pump capture?
options: Exhaust from the car's tailpipe while the engine idles
Sulfur dioxide from the gasoline in the pump hose
Particles of dust from the station forecourt
Gasoline vapor pushed out as the tank fills

why.correct: When you fill a tank, gasoline vapor (VOCs) is pushed out. The nozzle captures the vapor and returns it to the station's storage tank. It does not touch the car's exhaust.
options: This is the common mix-up; the nozzle never touches exhaust.
Gasoline is low in sulfur, and the nozzle captures vapor, not SO2.
The nozzle captures fuel vapor, not dust.
Right: it captures VOCs at the pump and returns them to storage.

items.q: A city wants to cut its NOx and VOCs from traffic without new technology on cars. Which approach fits best?
options: Require new catalytic converters on the cars sold in the city
Install scrubbers on the city's coal plant
Expand transit and bike lanes to cut driving
Build taller smokestacks at downtown factories

why.correct: Fewer vehicle miles means less NOx and VOCs. Better public transit and bike lanes cut driving without changing car technology.
options: That is a technology on cars, which the question rules out.
Scrubbers cut SO2 from coal plants, not NOx and VOCs from traffic.
Right: less driving means less NOx and VOCs.
Taller stacks spread pollution; they do not cut traffic emissions.

items.q: A cement plant releases 5,000 metric tons of particulates a year. A baghouse filter captures 99.5% of them. Write the setup for the particulates still released each year, then the answer.

why.correct: Released share: $100\% - 99.5\% = 0.5\%$. $5{,}000\,\text{t} \times \frac{0.5}{100} = 25$ metric tons a year.

mistakes.why: That is the amount captured. The question asks what is still released: 100% - 99.5% = 0.5%.
Divide the percent by 100 to turn it into a fraction.
4,975 metric tons is what the baghouse captures. Subtract it from 5,000 to get what is released.

items.q: Explain how a catalytic converter reduces smog, naming the pollutant it changes and what it becomes.

why.correct: The answer names a smog ingredient the device removes (NOx) and what it becomes (nitrogen gas), so it says how the benefit works.

specific.frame: A catalytic converter changes ___ into ___, which reduces smog because ___.

input.label: Pollutant changed
options: nitrogen oxides
sulfur dioxide
carbon dioxide

why.1: SO2 is removed from smokestacks by scrubbers, not by car converters.
why.2: The converter makes CO2; it does not remove it.

output.label: What it becomes
options: ozone
nitrogen gas and oxygen
nitric acid

why.0: Making ozone would add smog, not reduce it.
why.2: Nitric acid is a secondary pollutant; the converter makes harmless N2.

because.label: Why that reduces smog
options: less NOx is left to react with VOCs in sunlight to form ozone
nitrogen gas absorbs sunlight before it reaches the ground
the converter cools the air above the city

why.1: N2 does not block sunlight; the benefit is fewer ozone-making ingredients.
why.2: The converter does not change the air temperature.

specific.model: A catalytic converter changes nitrogen oxides into nitrogen gas and oxygen, which reduces smog because less NOx is left to react with VOCs in sunlight to form ozone.
